parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define electric potential at a point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
A hydrogen atom may be considered to consist of a proton and an electron separated by a distance of $120\text{ pm}$, as shown in Fig. 5.1.

{{figure:figure_5_1.png}}

The two particles may be considered as point charges.

Point P lies on the line joining the electron and the proton and is at a variable distance $x$ from the proton.
parts.text: Show that the electric potential $V$ at point P when $x = 10\text{ pm}$ is equal to $130\text{ V}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Calculate, to two significant figures, $V$ when $x = 30\text{ pm}$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: On Fig. 5.1, draw a cross $(\times)$ at one position, other than infinity, where the electric potential is zero.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
On Fig. 5.2, sketch the variation of $V$ with $x$ between $x = 10\text{ pm}$ and $x = 110\text{ pm}$.

{{figure:figure_5_2.png}}
